beats.text: There's no such thing as a normal vulva. Scientists measured it!
Swiss gynecologists measured six hundred fifty-seven women, aged fifteen to eighty-four.
The inner labia ranged from five millimeters to ten centimeters. The outer ones: from about one to eighteen centimeters. So what's normal?
All of it! Every single one!
And by the way: what you see is the vulva. The vagina is inside!
So if yours looks different: that's the normal part.

sources: Kreklau, Vâz, Oehme, Strub, Brechbühl, Christmann & Günthert (2018), Measurements of a 'normal vulva' in women aged 15–84: a cross-sectional prospective single-centre study, BJOG 125(13) – 657 women, Lucerne: labia minora 5–100 mm, labia majora 12–180 mm.
Lloyd, Crouch, Minto, Liao & Creighton (2005), Female genital appearance: 'normality' unfolds, BJOG 112(5) – 50 women: labia minora length 20–100 mm, width 5–60 mm.
